When Bitcoin can enforce where an output is spent (CTV, `OP_CAT`, `OP_CHECKSIGFROMSTACK` or an
equivalent), a cBTC lock becomes a vault that only a redemption opens, minted with no bond behind it.
The bytes are already reserved ([`SPEC.md` §10](../SPEC.md#10-extensions-and-covenant-placeholders)).

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge]
A liquidity provider (LP) swaps the same asset across Bitcoin and Ethereum with an adaptor-signature atomic swap, so a
holder of TAC on Bitcoin has TAC in the Ethereum pool in about the time of one Bitcoin block and one Ethereum settle,
instead of waiting for the reflection. The reflection bridge is unchanged: the LP rebalances over it, off the user's
clock.

Neither party holds the other's funds at any point. Each leg is enforced by its own chain: a Taproot script on
Bitcoin, the pool's lock set on Ethereum. The only thing that links them is a secret `t`.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > A swap, Bitcoin to Ethereum
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > A swap, Bitcoin to Ethereum]
1. The LP publishes its Bitcoin claim key and a quote (amount in, amount out, windows, and `takeSats`, the fee of its take:

   `546 + 750 vB × 2 × the fee rate`, which the user's client accepts up to 30,000 sats).

2. The user picks a note, derives `t` and `T = t·G` from its key and the note's outpoint, and moves the amount into a

   Taproot output keyed `P_LP + T` with a refund leaf `<csv> OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY OP_DROP <user> OP_CHECKSIG`. A

   sealed OP_RETURN in the same transaction lets the user find the lock again from its key, and an output of `takeSats`

   pays for the take, so a provider needs no Bitcoin of its own: by the time it takes, that output is confirmed with the

   lock. The LP refuses a lock that does not pay it. The output is one of two kinds. A provider that says `takeInLock` in its

   quote (`FB_LP_TAKE_IN_LOCK=on`) is paid by a second output of the lock's own script: only its key with `t` opens it (it

   sweeps it to its own address first and takes the note with that coin), and the user's refund leaf opens it too, so the

   take is the provider's when the swap is done and the user's when it is not. Any other provider is paid by a plain output

   to its own address, which it keeps if the user refunds; a page uses the first kind only when the quote asks for it, and a

   provider answers either kind.

3. The user sends the LP its lock offer. The LP reads the lock from the chain: the transaction and the notes it

   spends, the note the validator derives, its asset and commitment, its confirmations, and whether a spent note is

   already consumed on Ethereum.

4. After the confirmations its policy asks for, the LP moves a pool note of exactly the amount into the pool's lock

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > A swap, Bitcoin to Ethereum
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > A swap, Bitcoin to Ethereum]
set under `(T, deadline, recipient = the user's claim key)` and sends the user the lock terms and a

   pre-signature of the claim kernel, adapted to `T`.

5. The user finds the lock in the pool, checks the pre-signature, and claims: the kernel completes with `t`, and the

   claim's public values carry the completed signature `z`.

6. The LP reads `z` from the settle, computes `t = z − s̃` and spends the Bitcoin lock by key path with `d_LP + t`.

If a party stops, each side refunds on its own: the LP's lock after the Ethereum deadline, the user's lock after the
Bitcoin timelock. Ethereum to Bitcoin is the same swap with the roles exchanged: the LP holds `t` and locks Bitcoin
first, the user locks the pool note.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > What each side reads from the chain
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > What each side reads from the chain]
Nothing in an offer stands in for a chain read. The Ethereum locker takes the swap id from the outpoint the lock
transaction spends, the note and its asset from the validator, the confirmations from the chain, the lock output's
script from the transaction, and whether the spent notes are consumed on Ethereum from the pool. The Bitcoin locker
accepts an Ethereum offer only when the lock leaf is in the pool's lock set, the leaf recomputes from the stated
terms, and the pre-signature verifies against the output it chose. A pre-signature over `(L − O)` exists only if the
locked note holds exactly the quoted amount.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider]
Nothing in the pool or the swap is specific to one provider: a provider is a Tacit key with private TAC that answers a user's requests and takes the Bitcoin. Providers find users, and users find them, without a server of
the provider's own:

- **An ad.** A provider signs an ad with its claim key: its terms (fee, limits, timelock), what it can take now, and the gateway

  key requests are sealed to. An ad stands for a few minutes and is posted again every minute. A user's page checks each

  ad's signature itself, whoever delivered it. An ad has the members `AD_MEMBERS` lists (`dapp/fastbridge-board.js`) and no

  others, and a name of plain text (no `<` or `>`, no control characters): the board and every page refuse one that does not, so

  a program that reads the board's `/ads` can rely on that, though it should still escape what it shows. A new member goes in

  that list first, and a provider posts it once the board and the pages know it.

- **A board.** The ads are posted to a small board, which also carries requests and answers: a request is sealed to the

  provider's gateway key and an answer to the request's one-time key (the private route's sealing, `dapp/sealed-request.js`),

  and only the provider the request was for can post its answer. The board can drop or delay a message and can read, change

  or answer none. The requests are the ones of the HTTP API, so a provider in a browser tab, which cannot serve a request,

  answers what a daemon does. A provider that serves HTTP can be listed directly as well.

- **A choice.** The page asks every provider that can take the amount for a quote, shows the best, and asks the next best

  when the first cannot hold the payout.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider]
- **A split.** When no one provider takes the amount whole but the providers that take any TAC hold it between them, the fast page splits

  it (`dapp/fast/sweep.js`, `sweepOffer` and `startSweep` in `dapp/fast/wire.js`, `sweep` in `dapp/fastbridge-client.js`): at most four parts,

  planned for the least fee kept (each provider gives its least and the cheapest rate is filled first; a part costs a small fixed amount in the

  ranking, so a plan with fewer parts wins when it costs almost the same). Each part is a whole swap of its own, quoted by its own provider for its own

  amount, locked from notes of its own with its own refund, so one that stops costs the others nothing. Every part's payout is held by its

  provider before the first lock is built, so a provider that cannot hold its share is found out while the TAC is still in hand and nothing has

  been sent; the page then plans the split again without it. The parts are then locked one at a time, each leaving alone the fee coins the parts

  before it spent (`feeInputs` on each swap's record). A part that cannot be started after another has been leaves that one under way, and the page

  says how much was not. Each part is listed as "Part n of m" (`sweep` on the record). A lock spends notes whole and what is left of one comes back

  unconfirmed, so a split needs a note for each part (the page says so when the key's TAC is in too few) and a confirmed fee coin for each lock.

- **A wait.** When no provider online takes the amount, and it cannot be split either, the page keeps a want for the key in the browser and posts it to the

  boards, signed by a key made for it alone, for up to a day. Providers see what is waiting (the provider panel, and an alert in

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider]
the daemon); the holder is told on `/fast/`, and on the front page once, when a provider can take it. A want moves nothing.

  A want may also name the most its holder will pay, `maxFeeBps` (what the provider keeps, its rate and its flat part together, as hundredths of a percent

  of the amount; whole numbers from 0 to 10000, the page asks for 0 to 90%). The field is optional and is signed with the rest, so no one on the way can

  change it; a want that names none is the want it was before prices, byte for byte, and any fee the page quotes will do. The price is the demand a

  provider sees: the panel shows it beside the size and counts a want as one this key can take only when the fee it would keep is within it ("N more at a lower

  fee" says how many it would take at a lower one), and the daemon's alert says what they pay at most and how many its own fee meets. The holder is told

  only of a provider that keeps no more than the price (`meetsPrice`, `dapp/fastbridge-board.js`, the one judgement every page and the daemon use; it

  is the provider's own sum, `feeOf`, so a want is judged as the quote will be), and the page says when every provider that could take it asks more.

  A board needs no change for prices: it keeps a want as it came, and a reader that does not know the field leaves it out.

- **Depth.** `/fast/` has a section, closed until opened and needing no key, that lays the providers out as a ladder (`dapp/fast/ladder.js`): what each

  size costs, from the least any provider takes through round sizes (10, 30, 100, 300, 1,000 TAC and on) to the most that can be had now, as the page would

  bridge it. A provider's fee is a rate and a flat part, so the cost of a size is a curve and the cheapest provider changes with it; a size one provider

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider]
takes whole goes to the cheapest of those that do, and a size none takes whole is split (the row says across whom), so the ladder shows what the page

  will do and not a cheaper split it would not. Below it, what is waiting for a provider, grouped by the price it will pay (those that name none first, then

  the highest price down), read from the boards when the section opens and each minute while it stays open. It is a view of what the quotes will say, not a

  book that matches anything: a bridge still runs by asking a provider for a quote.

A provider in a page is for modest amounts: it answers requests and takes the Bitcoin while the page is open, and swaps that
are open when the page closes are tended again the next time the key is opened. A provider that is a process (`fastbridge-lp/`)
keeps them tended without a page.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider]
**Which notes a provider can take.** A lock's notes need only be valid Tacit notes, the validator's verdict, and that includes a
note made by an exit from the Bitcoin shielded pool (`T_BTC_SPEND`, opcode 0x6d). Such a note cannot be bridged home by burning
it: the burn's proof follows transfers back to the etch and does not follow a history through the pool. TAC a provider takes this
way stays on Bitcoin, where it can be traded. A provider that rebalances by bridging home screens locks with the regular
bridge's own trace (`POST /reflection/burndep/trace` answers a note like this with "opcode 0x6d") and refuses such a lock after it is
on Bitcoin, when its fees are spent and its TAC waits out the timelock. The reference provider takes any TAC the validator accepts, and says so:
its `/info` and its signed ad carry `anyTac: true`. A provider that says nothing of it is taken to screen. A provider run from the
`/fast/` page has a switch for it ("Take TAC that came out of the shielded pool", on by default): switched off, it leaves `anyTac` out
of its terms and refuses a lock that spends a note the bridge's proof cannot follow, before it takes the lock (`policy.screen` in
`dapp/fastbridge-el.js`, built from the same check the page uses). The LP daemon has no such switch: it takes any TAC and says so.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Anyone can be the provider]
The holder never picks a kind of TAC. The page sends each lock to the best provider that takes what it must spend (`begin` in
`dapp/fast/wire.js`). Notes the proof follows go to any provider; a provider that screens is given only such notes, looked at before
the lock is built with the trace (`lineage` in `dapp/burndep-ux.js`; a note the reflection tracks needs no trace, and a trace that
cannot be read stops the lock rather than guess). Notes it cannot follow (a pool or farm trade, an exit from the shielded pool, TAC
that came over from Ethereum) go only to a provider that takes any TAC, and the page passes over a better quote from a provider that
screens for one that does. When no provider online takes what must be spent, the page says so and locks nothing. A history longer
than the proof folds (255 transfers) is not looked at this way: the trace's verdict on it is a limit and not a refusal, and whether a
provider takes it is the provider's rule. The Bridge tab offers the fast bridge for a note the regular bridge cannot follow when a
provider online takes any TAC.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > On the front page
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > On the front page]
The Bridge tab's way in for TAC from Bitcoin prefers the fast bridge: when a note is picked, the tab asks the providers there are
(`dapp/fast/lp.json`, the boards) whether one takes that amount now. If one does, the tab quotes the bridge through the best of them
(`dapp/fast/route.js`): what arrives, the provider's fee, the Bitcoin cost (the lock is built and signed as a dry run, so an address that
cannot pay for it is told before the press), about how long it takes, and what happens if the provider stops. The first press says that and
locks nothing; the same press again begins the bridge with exactly the note picked. The regular bridge (a burn and the reflection, a few
hours, no provider fee) stays one press away under the receipt, and is the way when no provider takes the size, with the reason in its
receipt. The steps of a bridge through a provider are taken while any page of the site is open with the key (one tab at a time holds the
lock), and a bridge that ends is said once. `?fast=0` turns the preference off in a browser (`?fast=1` on again).

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Rules that keep a swap whole
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Rules that keep a swap whole]
- The counterparty's Bitcoin claim key is fixed before `t` exists, and the lock is built to that key.

- Each swap has exactly one Ethereum lock, and no two locks share an `L`: the claim kernel is over `(L, O)`. The

  Ethereum locker derives the blinding of `L` from its seed, the swap id and the whole adaptor point. It computes the

  Ethereum deadline once, from the block time at which the Bitcoin lock reached its confirmations, and stores it with the

  swap. A lock that is stored is sent from its stored bytes; a lock that may already be in the pool is looked up by its

  leaf before anything new is built; a lock that is found too late to answer is still watched and refunded. The record

  of an open swap is the safety state of the Ethereum locker and is kept durably and backed up. An offer that reaches

  the Ethereum locker long after its lock confirmed is not answered, which bounds what a lost record can lead to.

- The Ethereum locker takes only what it can lock. A quote checks its inventory and holds nothing; a reservation holds the

  payout when the user commits, before it locks any Bitcoin, and is extended once the lock is on the network and held

  through its confirmation. An offer whose payout is not held is held at that moment or declined. A provider that is out of

  inventory is therefore found out while the user's TAC is still in hand.

- Steps of one swap run one at a time, so overlapping ticks never build the same transaction twice.

- The Ethereum locker answers an offer only for a lock with a confirmation (a lock in the mempool can be replaced), checks the outpoint's

  shape and the amounts against the quote before it asks any explorer, and ends a swap whose lock does not reach its confirmations in time.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Rules that keep a swap whole
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Rules that keep a swap whole]
- A lock that is built again (the relay lost the job, or said it failed) is built from the note the first try used, so that if the first lands

  after all the second cannot: two locks of one swap would insert one leaf twice and strand a note. A note no longer held is waited for, not

  replaced, since the pool then shows the first lock by its leaf.

- What a settle did is read only from a settle the pool or its relayer was called with. Bytes that look like a settle inside the calldata of

  another contract's call are whatever their sender wrote.

- A stored take or refund whose funding coin was spent elsewhere is built again once it has had time to spread.

- A provider holds a payout for a swap, not for a quote: an offer is held at its arrival, under the lock that checks capacity, so two offers

  arriving together cannot both be given what is left for one. A reservation is extended once, by a transaction that pays the take, and one

  transaction stands for one quote.

- A lock is made from a pool note of exactly the amount. When there is none, one is cut from a larger note, once, and

  the tries that follow are spaced by growing waits, since each reads the wallet's notes.

- No claim is built with less than `minClaimSecs` left before the deadline: a claim that is sent and misses the

  deadline still publishes `t`.

- Time on Ethereum is the latest block's timestamp. The Ethereum locker refunds only after the deadline plus a margin,

  and looks for a claim again before every refund step, so a claim that lands near the deadline still opens the

  Bitcoin lock.

- Once the Bitcoin timelock has run, the Bitcoin locker takes its note back from any waiting phase, so a claim job

  that never answers or an offer that cannot be read does not hold it.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Rules that keep a swap whole
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Rules that keep a swap whole]
- The Ethereum locker signs its take over the sats value the lock output really carries, read from the transaction.

- Every field of an offer is checked for shape before it is used; a field that does not parse is refused with a reason.

- The pre-signature nonce binds the excess, `(L, O)`, the full compressed `T` and the lock leaf.

- Every record is stored before the step that sends it, and the step is resumed from the stored bytes.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Windows
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Windows]
| | default |
|---|---|
| Bitcoin refund timelock | 144 blocks |
| Ethereum lock window | 4 h from the block that confirmed the Bitcoin lock, rounded up to 10 min |
| Minimum time left to claim | 1 h |
| Offers answered | up to 1 h after the lock's first confirmation (`maxOfferAgeSecs`); the reference provider allows 2 h, since a lock needing three confirmations can have its third after an hour when blocks are slow |
| Slack between the Ethereum deadline and the opening of the Bitcoin refund | 2 h |
| Confirmations before the LP locks | policy by amount (1 for small, more for large) |

`checkEvmDeadline` and `btcRefundOpensAt` in `dapp/adaptor-xswap.js` hold the arithmetic: the Bitcoin refund must open
at least the slack after the Ethereum deadline, and the Ethereum locker needs time to see `z` and get its Bitcoin
claim mined before then.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Proving the claim
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Proving the claim]
The claim's proof is made by someone who sees `z` before the claim lands. The claimer therefore chooses its prover:
its own machine, its own credit on a prover network, or a relay that is not the LP. Adaptor jobs are not offered to the
open proof board for the same reason. `adaptorlock` and `adaptorclaim` are expiring job types in the relay, so a relay
that is paused or held skips a job whose deadline has passed instead of sending it.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Without a provider: TAC made ready
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Without a provider: TAC made ready]
A holder can also skip the provider. One Bitcoin transaction binds TAC to the pool (`T_CXFER_BOUND`, 0x39): the notes it makes
sit at the key's Taproot address, keyed to it, with blindings from the key's own change channel, so the key alone finds and
opens them again. Once the reflection has folded that transaction (24 blocks, then its proof), each bound note moves into the
pool by the fast lane (SPEC §6.3) in one settle: a transfer whose input is proven in the reflected Bitcoin root and absent from
the reflected spent set, signed by the note's Taproot key. The relay settles it for a fee taken from the note, so no ETH is
needed. The wait is paid once, when the TAC is made ready, not when it moves.

- `dapp/btc-bind.js`: the bind (`bindTransfer`, at most 8 notes of chosen sizes), `openBoundNote`, and `fastLaneNote`, which asks

  `POST /reflection/note-witness` (leaves and nullifiers) and checks its roots against the pool's (`knownBitcoinRoot`, slot 78,

  and `knownBitcoinSpentRoot`, slot 79) before anything is proven; a settle against any other spent root reverts.

- `dapp/fast/wire.js` `openBound` and `dapp/fast/bound.js`: the "Ready for Ethereum" panel on `/fast/`, unlisted while it is

  new (only `/fast/#ready` shows it), 10 to 1,000 TAC a bind. A bind spends the key's tracked TAC at its trading address and,

  where they are, the TAC that came back from Ethereum (cross-out mints at its Taproot address, spent by key path).

- Rules that keep it whole: a bound note is never a lot (a purchase refuses it), since its holder could still move it to Ethereum

  and void the buyer's side until the reflection passes the spend; a note bound to a pool the wallet cannot read is pending; the

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Without a provider: TAC made ready
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Without a provider: TAC made ready]
Bitcoin shielded pool's replay refuses any input whose history holds a bound note. A transfer out of a bound note is pending

  until the reflection passes its block, so a provider's lock check already refuses a lock that spends one too early.

- A bridge to Bitcoin can arrive ready (`crossout-ux.js` `start({ ready })`, the front page's "Arrive ready to come back fast",

  offered and ticked by default in a browser that has opened `/fast/#ready`, unless the holder last unticked it). It arrives when

  its mint is credited, like any bridge; then, under the open key, the page's bridge tick binds what it minted where it landed

  (`bindNow`, key path at the Taproot address, a failure kept as `bindError` and rested), so the TAC is ready about four hours

  later with no step of the holder's. The pool and guests are unchanged: a cross-out still mints an ordinary note.

- "Use on Bitcoin" turns a bound note back into ordinary TAC at the trading address (`unbindTransfer`, a plain transfer by key

  path, opened by the wallet's own change channel), usable on Bitcoin once the reflection passes it.

- Limits that stay, the pool and guests being kept as they are: the fast lane's signature has no deadline, a bound note names one

  pool deployment, and a fast-lane spend made while a reflection proof is out makes that proof stale (it is proven again). Binds

  are kept small (10 to 1,000 TAC) for that reason.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Known limits
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Known limits]
- A split goes only to providers that take any TAC (`anyTac`), because a part is not looked at note by note for a history the bridge's proof follows;
  a provider that screens takes whole bridges only. It is on the fast page: the front page's Bridge tab says the fast page can try splitting
  an amount that no one provider takes, and leaves the rest to it. The parts are taken from the largest providers' room as advertised, then quoted
  for real, so a provider that has less than it said is left out and the split planned again (three tries).
- A provider prices as it likes. A bridger's client quotes a fee up to 90% of the amount and flags one over 5% (`highFee`): the fast page
  says so in the receipt and at the first press, and the front page's Bridge tab keeps the regular bridge as its choice and says the fast
  page can still do it (`dapp/fast/fmt.js`, `route.js`). A fee over 90% is not quoted.

- A board is a memory-only relay: it can be filled with junk requests (64 for each provider for ten minutes) and its ad slots with

  throwaway keys. An ad is signed by the claim key only, so a provider whose ad has lapsed can have its gateway key named in an ad of

  someone else's until that one lapses. Both need a change to the ad's format (a gateway signature) and a deploy of the board and the pages

  together; the board's runs now carry an id, so a provider reads again from the start after a board restart.

- The quotes of a provider are kept until two days after they ran out; the file store reads every record for each capacity check.

- The pre-signature is served to anyone who asks after the pool lock is made; a lock that is reorganised away after the provider's

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Known limits
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Known limits]
confirmations (one for the smaller amounts) can be double-spent by its maker. The confirmations policy is the defence.

- The claim's proof is made by the claimer's chosen prover; see "Proving the claim".

- Wants cost nothing to make up: the board takes 30 an hour from one address (`fastbridge-lp/board.mjs`, which needs

  `FB_BOARD_TRUST_PROXY` behind a reverse proxy to tell addresses apart), and a provider's panel lists each by size with how many it can take.

- When the relay is held (it proves but does not send), the pages send each settle from the

  connected Ethereum wallet after 45 s (`fastbridge-evm.js` jobStatus, `fast/wire.js` walletSettle): an open-board job with its proof, and

  an adaptor lock, claim or refund (which never go on the open board) proved again prove-only. The sender's address is public on

  Ethereum, so a bridger who sends its own claim links that address to the claim; the wallet asks first. `tests/fastbridge-fork.mjs` C

  runs a whole swap this way through the settle guest on a fork.

- The device prover does not take the adaptor ops yet (`device-prover.js` DEVICE_TYPES). Nothing in them goes stale while a laptop

  proves (the pool accepts any lock-set root it has known), so adding them is a matter of wiring and a guest run on the device.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Status
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Status]
Live on mainnet: the bridge page (`/fast/`) and the front page's Bridge tab, with providers found through the board named in
`dapp/fast/lp.json`.

Built and tested: the protocol (its messages in both directions, `tests/adaptor-xswap.test.mjs`), the transaction builders,
both role machines, a simulated chain, the full swap Bitcoin to Ethereum against the real settle guest and the real note
validator (`tests/fastbridge-fork.mjs`), the pool adapter, the LP process with its HTTP API, store and explorer adapter,
the board and the mailbox over it, and the bridge page (`/fast/`) with its client, recovery from the key, a choice
among providers, a provider mode for any key, and a browser check. The page reads its board from `dapp/fast/lp.json`.

chunks.title: FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Status
chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Status]
Ethereum to Bitcoin: the two machines, unchanged and with the roles swapped (the LP the Bitcoin locker, the user the
Ethereum locker), complete a whole swap in the simulated chain, and the LP takes its Bitcoin note back by the timelock when
the user never locks (`tests/fastbridge-reverse.test.mjs`; that chain mirrors the pool's checks in JS). A provider's reverse
service and the user's client over those machines (`tests/fastbridge-reverse-service.test.mjs`, same chain) complete a swap whose
two amounts differ by the provider's fee, refuse what they should (a key that is not a key, an amount out of range or with no TAC
behind it, a quote that is not for the user, a lock by another key), keep a stranger's offer out, survive a provider restart, and
bound what a stream of requests can tie up. Not run for this direction: the real settle guest, and most of the failure cases the
other direction has (a user silent after the provider locks is covered; slow confirmations, a claim that fails to land, a pool lock
refunded after the provider claimed late, dishonest offers are not).

The provider process can run the reverse service (`FB_LP_REVERSE=on`, off by default; `fastbridge-lp/README.md`, "Selling the other way"): it
derives a Bitcoin address of its own from the provider's key, reads the confirmed TAC at that address, bounds the sends at once and the TAC out at once,
answers `/reverse/...` next to the forward routes, and, started with a throwaway key and nothing funded, answers `/reverse/info` (`available: 0`) from that
address, a different one from its main address. It has not been run against a funded address, a real swap, or the real settle guest.

chunks.text:
[FAST-BRIDGE.md > Fast bridge > Status]
A provider that runs it says so in its ad (a `reverse` member with that direction's terms, signed with the rest, read from `/reverse/info`), and the /fast/ page
(`fast/reverse.js`, wired by `openReverse` in `fast/wire.js`) shows a "Send TAC to Bitcoin" panel only when a listed provider's ad has one: it quotes the cheapest
provider with room, shows what is sent and what arrives on Bitcoin, starts the swap, and tends every provider it has asked (the providers are remembered in this
browser, so a swap that outlasts the page is tended again when it opens). Until a provider is switched on and funded, nothing on the page changes.

Not built: the claim prover's options (the relay that is not the provider, the user's device, a prover network).

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops]
Bitcoin's state reaches Ethereum through calls anyone can make: block headers into the header relay, proofs of
each batch into the pool, and the open board's settles into the pool for the fees their proofs pay. Tacit's own
services make every one of them. So can you, from a browser wallet on
[tacit.finance/prove](https://tacit.finance/prove/) (its Relay and Bitcoin tabs), or from your own machine with one key and the
**community runner**, [`tools/community-runner.mjs`](../tools/community-runner.mjs).

The page and the runner build the same calls from the same modules:
[`dapp/header-relay-advance.js`](../dapp/header-relay-advance.js) for headers and
[`dapp/community-ops.js`](../dapp/community-ops.js) for proofs and the board.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Run it
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Run it]
Node 22 or later. Node 20 runs everything but the Nostr board unless started with `--experimental-websocket`.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/src-company/tacit
cd tacit && npm ci --omit=dev
DRY_RUN=1 ONCE=1 node tools/community-runner.mjs           # what it would send now; no key needed
RUNNER_KEY=0x… node tools/community-runner.mjs             # all three modes, each on its own loop
RUNNER_KEY=0x… node tools/community-runner.mjs settles     # one mode: headers, attest or settles
node tools/community-runner.mjs mirror                       # keep the board public on Nostr; no key, no gas
FORWARD_URL=https://your.host node tools/community-runner.mjs forward   # carry private requests; no key, no gas (needs a public https address)
```

Use a fresh key that holds only ETH for gas. The board pays its fees to the sending account, and an account with
code (an EIP-7702 delegation) runs that code on them; the runner says so at start when the key has code.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Run it
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Run it]
| env | default | |
|---|---|---|
| `RUNNER_KEY` | | The account that signs, pays the gas and is paid the board's fees. Not needed with `DRY_RUN=1`. |
| `RPC_URL` | `https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com` | Reads and simulation. |
| `SEND_RPC_URL` | `https://rpc.flashbots.net/fast?hint=hash` | Where signed transactions go. Flashbots Protect does not include a transaction that would revert, and keeps it out of the public mempool. |
| `API_BASE` | `https://api.tacit.finance` | Published proofs, the board, landings. |
| `ESPLORA_URL` | `https://blockstream.info/api` | Bitcoin's headers. |
| `DRY_RUN=1` | | Simulate and print what would be sent; send nothing. |
| `ONCE=1` | | One pass of each mode, then exit (status 1 if a pass failed). |
| `HEADERS_SECS` `ATTEST_SECS` `SETTLES_SECS` | 300, 60, 15 | Each mode's cadence. A pass that sent something, or passed over a job the pool refused, runs again at once. |
| `HEADERS_MIN_BEHIND` | 3 | See *headers*. |
| `HEADERS_NEED` | | A Bitcoin height to carry the relay to, whatever the pacing: a cBTC lock's or bridge deposit's block + 24. |
| `ATTEST_AFTER_SECS` | 120 | See *attest*. |
| `MARGIN_BPS` | 2000 | See *settles*. |
| `NOSTR` | 1 | Read and copy the board on public Nostr relays (see *settles*). 0: the API's board alone. |
| `NOSTR_RELAYS` | `wss://relay.damus.io`, `wss://nos.lol`, `wss://relay.primal.net`, `wss://offchain.pub` | Comma separated. |
| `MAX_GAS_GWEI` | 5 | Headers, attests and ancestry calls wait while the base fee is above this. 0 turns the ceiling off. |
| `PRIORITY_GWEI` | 0.1 | The tip each transaction offers. |

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Run it
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Run it]
Every transaction is run against the latest block from the runner's own address before it is signed, and its gas
limit comes from the node's estimate. Transactions go one at a time; each is waited for (up to 3 minutes) before
the next. Work someone else finished meanwhile is passed over: a header batch already on the relay, a proof the
pool has moved past, a settle another sender landed.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > headers
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > headers]
Sends Bitcoin's block headers, read from the explorer, to `BitcoinLightRelay.advanceTip`, at most 40 a
transaction. The relay checks each header's proof of work, and the runner refuses to extend a relay whose tip is
not the explorer's block at that height (a fork needs an operator).

- **When.** The next proof is waiting on the relay (the relay has not confirmed past the proven block) and the relay
  is at least `HEADERS_MIN_BEHIND` blocks behind Bitcoin's tip less 2. Tacit's own relay usually keeps within a
  block or two, so the runner sends when it falls behind. It advances as far as the reflection can use soon:
  Bitcoin's tip less 2, or the proven block + 24 + 110, whichever is lower.
- **Costs.** About 92,000 gas a transaction plus 172,000 a header (15 headers estimated 2.68 million gas).
- **Earns.** Nothing on chain. It keeps bridge deposits and cBTC locks moving.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > attest
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > attest]
Lands a proof of Bitcoin's state that Tacit's prover has published (`GET /reflection/proof`) and not landed, with
`ConfidentialPool.attestBitcoinStateProven(publicValues, proof)`.

- **When.** The proof still builds on the pool's attested digest, and it was published at least
  `ATTEST_AFTER_SECS` ago. Tacit's prover lands its own proofs, usually within that time.
- **Ancestry.** While the proofs are more than 2,016 blocks behind the relay's confirmed tip, no batch can reach
  them, so this mode calls `advanceReflectionAncestry()` first: each call walks up to 2,016 of the relay's blocks
  toward a checkpoint the next batch can build on, and the runner calls it until the gap closes.
- **Costs.** An attest uses about 0.4 to 0.6 million gas (a recent one used 419,593). An ancestry call walks up to
  2,016 relay blocks and costs more; its estimate is logged before it is sent.
- **Earns.** Nothing on chain. Bridge deposits up to the proven block can mint once it lands.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > settles
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > settles]
Sends the open board's settles with `ConfidentialPool.settle(publicValues, proof, memos)`. The board is read from
two places, and either one alone is enough:

- Tacit's API (`GET /confidential/open`, see [OPEN-RELAYER.md](./OPEN-RELAYER.md)). A landing is reported back
  (`POST /confidential/landed`).
- Public Nostr relays: proofs that holders, /prove/ tabs and other runners posted there
  ([`dapp/nostr-board.js`](../dapp/nostr-board.js)). Each pass also copies the API's open jobs that no relay carries
  yet, so the board stays public if the API stops answering. A job read from Nostr alone needs no report: the chain
  is its record.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > settles
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > settles]
- **When.** A job is open (no other sender has taken it), whole, and more than two minutes from its deadline, by
  the latest block's time. Of those, the runner takes the oldest whose fee pays its gas with `MARGIN_BPS` to
  spare: first at 600,000 gas, then again at the job's own estimate. A job the pool refuses in simulation is passed
  over for ten minutes.
- **What a fee is worth.** tETH legs at their face value in ETH. TAC legs at 80% of the TAC/tETH pool's spot price,
  read from the pool's reserves at most once a minute. The discount covers the price risk of being paid in TAC.
  Moving that price far enough to fool a sender costs more than the gas a sender could lose.
- **Costs.** A recent transfer's settle used 348,054 gas; the runner prices a job at 600,000 before its own estimate.
- **Earns.** Each fee leg the proof binds, paid to the sending account inside the same transaction: tETH legs as
  ETH, TAC legs as TAC. A fork of mainnet replaying a real settle paid the runner its 0.0062 ETH fee less 0.000084 ETH
  of gas. Legs in other assets are paid too but are not counted when choosing what to send. Jobs reach the board when
  Tacit's relay has proved a settle it is not sending yet, or when a holder posts a proof made with their own prover
  (tacit.finance offers this when its relay is not proving: the holder's computer proves the action with a fee for
  its sender). Tacit's relay sends its own as soon as it can, so the first sender is paid.
- The board API allows a burst of 30 reads and one every 2 seconds after that, per IP address.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > mirror (opt-in, not part of `all`)
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > mirror (opt-in, not part of `all`)]
Copies the API's open jobs to the Nostr relays, as *settles* does on each pass, and sends nothing. It needs no key
and no gas, so anyone can keep the board public. Up to four jobs a minute, each posted once an hour.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > forward (opt-in, not part of `all`)
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > forward (opt-in, not part of `all`)]
A forwarder for the EVM pool's private route (docs/EVM-POOL.md, "Private route"). A wallet seals each request to a keeper's gateway key and sends
it to a forwarder; the forwarder hands it to the keeper's `POST /sealed` and returns the sealed answer. It sees the sender's address and the size and
time of each envelope, never what is in one; it holds no key, forwards nothing of the sender's and keeps nothing. It needs no key and no ETH.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > forward (opt-in, not part of `all`)
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > forward (opt-in, not part of `all`)]
- **Needs:** a public **https** address that reaches this machine: a VPS, or a machine behind a tunnel you run. A home connection with no way in cannot
  carry one. `PORT` (default 10000) is where it listens; put TLS in front of it.
- **Run:** `PORT=10000 FORWARD_URL=https://your.host node tools/community-runner.mjs forward`. With `FORWARD_URL` set it sends a sealed read to the keepers
  through that address, now and every fifteen minutes, and says whether it came back (and whether the browser's CORS check will pass).
- **Check it from outside:** `node tools/private-route-check.mjs --service https://tacit-evm-pool-keepers.onrender.com --gateway <the public key `GET /1/evm-pool/keeper/info` shows as `sealed.key`> --forwarder https://your.host` runs the checks a listing needs: health, the browser's CORS preflight, a burst of sealed reads that match the direct answers, and what the route refuses.
- **Join the list:** a page lists the forwarders it uses, so send the address to Tacit. A forwarder run by the keepers' own operator hides nothing from it,
  which is why the list should be independent operators.
- **Limits:** 60 requests a minute per sender (`FORWARDER_RATE_PER_MIN`). The keeper counts everything behind one forwarder as that forwarder's, so a
  forwarder that carries many people should be named in the keepers' `EVM_POOL_KEEPER_FORWARDERS`.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > relay-check (opt-in, not part of `all`)
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > relay-check (opt-in, not part of `all`)]
`node tools/community-runner.mjs relay-check https://relay.example/1/evm-pool/keeper` checks a Pay relay you run, the way a wallet reaches it: its quote names an
address, it shows a private route key signed for by that address, the relay registry lists it there, and a sealed quote comes back through Tacit's forwarders. It
needs no key and no ETH, says which step fails and what to do about it, and exits 1 if any does. How to run and list a relay: [RUN-A-PAY-RELAY.md](./RUN-A-PAY-RELAY.md).
A forwarder that also carries the relays the registry lists runs with `FORWARDER_RPC_URL` set (docs/EVM-POOL.md, "Relays from the registry").

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > board (opt-in, not part of `all`)
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > board (opt-in, not part of `all`)]
Race Tacit's own prover for the prover board's public jobs. These are plain wraps, whose program input holds no one's secret and tells a prover nothing the chain does not already show: the settle consumes one deposit and inserts that depositor's own note in the same transaction, for an amount the underlying transfer reveals. Ops that pay someone else are not raced, even though their inputs hold no secret either: an input carries the commitment and owner behind each leaf the pool publishes only as a hash, so whoever proves one would learn which inserted leaf is the recipient's and could follow it to the moment it is spent. Those are proved on a machine trusted with a witness, or by the payer ([Prove it yourself](#prove-for-the-wrap-pool)). `board` claims one at a time (`POST /prover/community/claim` with your address), proves it with `tacit-prover` beside it and hands the proof back. Claiming takes the job from no one: Tacit's worker goes on with it, the relay checks each proof that comes back as it checks its own (a simulated settle) and uses the first that passes. A proof that does not pass costs nothing but a mark on the board's summary against the address.

- **Needs:** `tacit-prover` running, and `MINER=0x…`, the address the board credits. No key and no ETH: nothing is sent on chain.

- **Who wins:** a press waits a few minutes at most, so a machine that proves in under a minute (a desktop GPU) wins races; a laptop's 10 to 15 minutes does not. After its first proof the runner passes over a job due sooner than its last proof took. Laptops earn more from [Prove for the wrap pool](#prove-for-the-wrap-pool), whose wraps wait.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > board (opt-in, not part of `all`)
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > board (opt-in, not part of `all`)]
- **Tacit chain blocks, by draw:** in an open race the fastest machine wins every block. With `PROVER_BOARD_BLOCK_DRAW_PCT` set (0, off, by default), that share of blocks is first offered to one machine picked by lottery, as a Bitcoin block goes to a miner with odds by hashpower. A place's odds are its speed: 1 ÷ its usual seconds per block, from the blocks the relay has taken from it, shown as `blocks`, `blockSecs` (proving) and `blockFelt` (the whole wait: the block posted, or opened to the race when the machine was not the one drawn, to its answer arriving) on `GET /prover/board`. The odds use the whole wait, so a machine that is slow to ask for work, or busy with another proof when a block is posted, weighs less than one with the same GPU that is not; a block drawn for a machine and taken from another counts its wait against that machine. Its proving time still sets the lease and when the race joins it. Only a machine that asked for work in the last 6 s (`PROVER_BOARD_BLOCK_DRAW_FRESH_MS`) is drawn: a machine busy with another proof, or asking less often than that, would not see the block inside its 15 s offer, and the user would wait the whole offer; it is drawn at the moments it happens to have asked just before. `PROVER_BOARD_BLOCK_DRAW_NEW` (15 by default) is the share of the odds kept for places with no record yet, so new machines can earn one, as long as the board has taken at least one proof of any kind from them. Those places take turns: `PROVER_BOARD_BLOCK_DRAW_SEATS` (3 by default) of them, the ones that have waited longest, hold a ticket at a time and split that share, and a place that is drawn goes to the back of the line (a block taken gives it a record, which sets its odds by speed from then on). A machine reads its place in the line as `line` on `GET /prover/board?address=…`. One ticket per place: more addresses on one connection buy no more odds. The block waits 15 s for the drawn machine to take it. Once the drawn machine passes 1.5 times its usual time (10 s at least, 30 s for a machine with no record), the race joins it: it keeps its claim and is still paid if it answers first, and being slow does not count against it. A lapse (three times its usual time: 20 s at least, 45 s with no record), a block given back or a wrong proof opens the block to the race, and that place goes after the others for a while. The fastest machine still wins most blocks, and the rest win their share and stay ready.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > board (opt-in, not part of `all`)
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > board (opt-in, not part of `all`)]
- **Points:** each proof the relay takes earns the address `POINTS_BOARD_PER_PROOF` points (20 by default; a Bitcoin-state batch earns 1,000 and a Tacit chain block 100), with no daily count unless `POINTS_BOARD_DAILY_CAP` sets one; a refused or unchecked proof earns nothing. The day's tally is at `GET /prover/board/credits?day=<n>`, the proof pool's shape. The points service's proof-mining campaign reads it beside the pool's and sums each address's points from both for the day.

- **Off:** `PROVER_BOARD_COMMUNITY=0` on the API closes the routes.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > Not included: overflow drains
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Modes > Not included: overflow drains]
`drainOverflow` and `drainOverflowRoots` apply effects a batch deferred past its per-attest cap. Their inputs are
the deferred items themselves (lock spends and redemptions, locks, asset metadata, calls) in the guest's committed
order, but an attest publishes only each chunk's running-keccak root. The items exist only inside the reflection
guest's run over that batch's Bitcoin blocks, which neither the chain nor the API publishes, so a runner cannot
build the call from public data. `pendingOverflowChunks()` on the pool reads 0 today.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Prove for the wrap pool
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Prove for the wrap pool]
A page with a Tacit account open asks the proof pool to keep wraps of a few sizes proved ahead, so the deposit that follows needs no wait for a proof. Any
computer can make those proofs. `tacit-prover` leases one wrap at a time from the pool (`GET /prover/pool`), proves it and sends the proof back; the API
keeps it only if its public values are the wrap's and the live SP1 verifier takes it, and credits the address you named with points. Tacit's own GPU
prover leaves a wrap to community provers first (up to ten minutes by default, and only while one has asked in the last five), so a computer that asks gets first pick.

```sh
curl -fsSL https://tacit.finance/prove.sh | sh -s -- 0xYourAddress    # install it and start it at login
curl -fsSL https://tacit.finance/prove.sh | sh -s -- --status         # running? what waits in the pool? what has the address earned?
curl -fsSL https://tacit.finance/prove.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall      # stop it and remove it
```

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Prove for the wrap pool
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Prove for the wrap pool]
[tacit prove](https://tacit.finance/prove/) gives the same command with your address filled in, then starts and pauses the installed prover and shows the
proof under way and what the address has earned (it talks to `tacit-prover` on 127.0.0.1: `GET /mine`, `POST /mine {miner, on}`, kept in
`~/.tacit-prover/mine.json`). [`dapp/prove.sh`](../dapp/prove.sh) picks the build
for the machine (an Apple-silicon Mac or x86-64 Linux; on Windows, run it inside WSL 2, see [On Windows](../contracts/sp1/confidential/device-prover/README.md#on-windows)), downloads the release it pins and runs nothing from it unless the
archive's sha256 is the pinned one, puts the program in `~/.tacit-prover/bin`, and sets it to start at login (a launchd agent, or a systemd user unit). Run
again, it updates the program and keeps the address. Cutting a new release means `node tools/prove-pins.mjs tacit-prover-vX.Y.Z`, which writes its sums into the script.

- **Needs:** about 8 GB of memory. The first proof downloads SP1's Groth16 circuit once, 6.2 GB (8.4 GB unpacked). A proof takes about 5 to 10 minutes on a Mac

  with 16 GB or more (13 minutes measured on an 8 GB MacBook Air) and uses the processor while it runs, so a laptop does best plugged in. The program makes one proof

  at a time and asks the pool for the next as soon as one is done (once a minute while the pool is empty).

- **Costs:** nothing else. No key and no ETH are involved and nothing is signed; the address only receives points. A proof it cannot make is handed back, unpaid.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Prove for the wrap pool
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > Prove for the wrap pool]
- **Earns:** up to 20 points a proof, with no daily count: a proof that comes back within a minute of its lease earns all 20, and one that takes longer earns less, in a straight line down to half (10 points) at ten minutes and beyond, so a laptop's proof still earns and a fast one earns more (`POOL_PAY_FULL_SECS` 60, `POOL_PAY_FLOOR_SECS` 600, `POOL_PAY_FLOOR_PCT` 50; 100 pays every proof the same; `GET /prover/pool` shows them as `terms.pay`). A job that came back (a lease ran out or was handed back) is timed by its age from the page's request instead, so taking up a job after a long wait earns at the floor. A lease held for 25 minutes (`POOL_HOUSE_TAKEOVER_MS`, 0 turns it off; `terms.takeoverSecs`) without a proof can be taken over by Tacit's own prover once it is free: the late proof is not taken, and the lapse counts against that place (a place is shut out for the UTC day at 4 lapses, `POOL_LAPSES_PER_DAY`; `GET /prover/pool` shows `lapsedToday`). A new job is held for 30 seconds for the place whose turn it is, a place's turn being one draw whatever addresses it asks under, an address's turns counting at most three of its places at once (`POOL_TICKETS_PER_ADDRESS`; `terms.ticketsPerAddress`), and a place with a lapse today going last. Once the day is over, the points service shares that day's TAC between the provers by points, no point

  paid more than a cap, so a proof pays up to 20 times the cap. [`GET https://tacit-points.onrender.com/mine`](https://tacit-points.onrender.com/mine) gives the

  terms, when they end and what is left in the pocket; add `?address=0x…` for what an address has been credited. [tacit prove](https://tacit.finance/prove/) and `--status` read it.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > On your device
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > On your device]
The runner makes no proofs; it lands proofs others publish. Proving an op with your own hardware is
[`contracts/sp1/confidential/device-prover/`](../contracts/sp1/confidential/device-prover/); proving with your own
Succinct account is in [OPEN-RELAYER.md](./OPEN-RELAYER.md#proving-with-your-own-prover-account).

A machine with an NVIDIA GPU runs the prover board's community worker with
`curl -fsSL https://tacit.finance/prove-gpu.sh | sh -s -- 0xYourAddress` ([tacit prove](https://tacit.finance/prove/) gives it with
your address filled in). It races the Tacit chain's blocks on the board ([`TACIT-BLOCKS.md`](./TACIT-BLOCKS.md)), proves the
proof pool's wraps between jobs, and on a card of 24 GB or more takes its turn at the board's Bitcoin-state batches. Each proof the
relay or the pool takes earns the address its points.

chunks.title: COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > On your device
chunks.text:
[COMMUNITY-OPS.md > Community ops > On your device]
`curl -fsSL https://tacit.finance/prove-gpu.sh | sh -s -- --status` says whether it is running and where it stands: the proofs the board
has taken from it, its Tacit chain block record (blocks taken, its usual time per block), how often it was drawn, and whether it is in
the [block draw](#board-opt-in-not-part-of-all) now with its odds, or, if not, why (not asking for work, or last asked more than 6 s ago, blocks switched off, no accepted
proof yet, a missed turn it is waiting out, a usual block time over 60 s, another machine on the same connection holding its one
ticket, or a place in the line of machines with no block record yet, with how many must be drawn before it holds a ticket). The same answer is `GET /prover/board?address=0x…` (JSON, or plain text with `&format=text`): the facts on the board's own
public summary, put in one place. A new machine needs one accepted proof of any kind, a wrap for the pool counts, before it holds a
ticket, and its odds start low and rise as its block record forms.
